_comment: Adjudicated repairs for Sets and Relations. Recurring defect class: 'Both A and B / All of the above' options whose letter references were written for a different option order (shuffle artifact) — repaired by naming contents instead of letters. Every entry re-derived by hand; the blind agent pass is corroborating evidence.

01-8.reason: Option A was an empty string (blank cell). Replaced with the closed-interval distractor [2,5]. Key B ([2,5)) verified correct for 2 ≤ x < 5.

01-9.reason: P(A), 𝒫(A) AND the old option D (℘(A)) are all accepted power-set notations, so 'All of the above' at position C was wrong-by-position (D sat below it and was also valid). D replaced with the complement notation (genuinely wrong); C reworded to name its contents. Key C retained.

01-13.reason: Keyed option A read 'Both A and B' — self-referential (it IS option A) and aimed at shuffled letters. Reworded to name the two empty-set notations (options B and C). Key A retained.

01-25.reason: Option C was truncated to ' for a set of integers' — the notation it was meant to display was missing. Restored as square-bracket misuse, which is the intended incorrect-notation answer. Key C retained.

01-27.reason: Old option D ('Interval (0,1)') was arguably ALSO correct — (0,1) denotes all reals, so it cannot express just the rationals. Replaced with a valid set-builder representation (clearly a wrong answer), leaving the keyed B (roster — impossible for a dense infinite set) uniquely correct.

01-28.stem: Which of these statements about the empty set is TRUE for every \(x\)?
01-28.solution: The empty set has no elements, so for every \(x\), \(x \notin \emptyset\) is true (and \(x \in \emptyset\) is always false).
01-28.reason: As printed ('the correct way to DENOTE x is an element of the empty set') the answer is the notation x ∈ ∅ (option C), but the key and teaching intent are the TRUE statement x ∉ ∅ (option B). Stem reworded to ask for the true statement, making key B correct and unambiguous.

02-26.reason: Options B ({∅}) and D ({{}}) were logically identical — {} IS ∅. D replaced with the power set of {∅} (a genuine distractor). Key B verified correct: P(∅) = {∅}.

03-27.solution: By inclusion–exclusion: \(90 = 40 + 50 + 30 - 15 - 10 - 12 + n(A \cap B \cap C) = 83 + n(A \cap B \cap C)\), so \(n(A \cap B \cap C) = 7\). (All seven Venn regions come out non-negative, so the data is consistent.)
03-27.reason: As printed (union = 100) the answer is 17, matching no option; the source solution asserted 7 with broken arithmetic. Stem repaired 100 → 90, which makes the keyed B (7) exactly correct and every Venn region non-negative (verified: singles 20/32/15, pairwise-only 8/3/5, triple 7, total 90).

04-14.reason: Key flip C→B: exactly-one = Σsingles − 2Σpairs + 3·triple = 230 − 210 + 60 = 80 — the source's OWN solution computes 35 + 25 + 20 = 80 and then trails off with 'Wait,'. Keyed C (85) matches nothing.

05-10.reason: Both printed identities (A×(B∩C) and A×(B∪C) distributivity) are true, and the keyed option read 'Both A and B' — letter references written for a different option order (B and D hold the identities here). A and C reworded to name contents. Key A retained.

06-3.solution: A relation from A to B must be a subset of \(A \times B = \{(1,3), (1,4), (2,3), (2,4)\}\). Only \(\{(1,3), (2,4)\}\) satisfies this — the other sets pair elements in the wrong order or are not sets of ordered pairs at all.
06-3.reason: Key D verified correct (agents agree); the source solution said 'Option A satisfies this condition' — a stale letter reference from a pre-shuffle option order. Reworded to name the set.

06-10.solution: A relation from \(\mathbb{R}\) to \(\mathbb{R}\) is formally a SET of ordered pairs, i.e. a subset of \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}\). The set-builder form \(\{(x,y) : y = x^2, x \in \mathbb{R}\}\) is exactly that; 'the parabola' and the bare equation \(y = x^2\) describe the relation informally but are not themselves sets of ordered pairs.
06-10.reason: Key A verified correct (agents agree); the source solution said 'Option B correctly represents…' — a stale letter reference. Reworded to name the representation.

07-3.solution: Reflexivity on \(\{1,2,3\}\) requires \((1,1), (2,2), (3,3) \in R\). Only \(R = \{(1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (1,2)\}\) contains all three diagonal pairs (extra pairs like \((1,2)\) do not break reflexivity).
07-3.reason: Key D verified correct (agents agree); the source solution said 'Only option C contains all these pairs' — a stale letter reference (C is {(1,2),(2,1)}). Reworded to name the relation.

07-7.reason: Old option A ({(1,2),(3,4)}) was VACUOUSLY transitive (no chainable pairs), making two correct options. Replaced with a chain missing its closure ((1,2),(2,3) but no (1,3) — genuinely not transitive). Key B verified correct.

07-15.reason: Both old A (7, 17, 27) and the keyed D (2, 12, 22) are ≡ 2 (mod 5) — two fully correct options. A replaced with the residue-3 list; key D retained (the canonical residue representatives, matching the source solution).

07-20.stem: For the relation \(R = \{(1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (1,2), (2,3), (1,3)\}\) on \(\{1, 2, 3\}\), which property does R NOT satisfy?
07-20.solution: R contains \((1,1), (2,2), (3,3)\) so it is reflexive, and every chain closes (\((1,2),(2,3) \to (1,3) \in R\)) so it is transitive. But \((1,2) \in R\) while \((2,1) \notin R\), so R is NOT symmetric.
07-20.reason: As printed R was ALSO not transitive ((1,2),(2,3) present but (1,3) missing), making options A and B both correct. Adding (1,3) to R makes it transitive and reflexive, leaving symmetry as the unique failing property — key A retained.

05-24.solution: \(A \times B = \{(1,2), (1,3)\}\), so \((A \times B) \times A = \{((1,2), 1), ((1,3), 1)\}\) — its elements have the form \(((a,b), c)\), and there are \(2 \times 1 = 2\) of them (not 6). Flat triples \((a,b,c)\) describe \(A \times B \times A\), a different (though naturally identified) construction.
05-24.reason: Key flip C→A: the keyed C read 'Both A and C' — self-referential shuffle artifact — while only A is true as printed (B's flat triples are a different construction; D's '6 elements' is false, there are 2). C replaced with a genuine distractor; waffling truncated solution rewritten.
